title: Philippines Social Commerce Operations
thesis: Snowflake turns daily live-selling activity from a synthetic Philippine retail social commerce network into clean-order and order-issue KPIs, 7-day returned-to-sender (RTS) risk scores, return rate anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on one governed platform.

talking_points: Clean order rate, order issues raised, RTS orders and GMV in PHP for 40 fictional live-selling creators in Quezon City, Cebu City, Davao City, Iloilo City and Cagayan de Oro.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to creator-day rows.
The issue-type chart shows which issues end as RTS orders, led by COD refused at door, and which are always resolved, such as courier network disruptions.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of social commerce KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which creators should the quality team watch first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each creator's probability of an RTS order in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent 14 labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags return rate outliers per creator, and the forecast projects network-wide order issues for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Are our creator controls keeping up?

talking_points: Catalog sync compliance, creator document coverage and pending documents frame the control gaps.
Catalog sync compliance against RTS orders by creator shows where missed catalog syncs before a livestream and RTS orders move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, creator, issue-type and risk tables only.
show: Catalog sync compliance and document coverage
Catalog sync compliance vs RTS orders
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when an order runs into an issue right now?

talking_points: Live livestream order events land in RAW.LIVE_ORDERS, from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ISSUE events with an SOP hint and the creator's current risk band, then emails the on-call analyst.
tabs.call_out: From order issue to creator case in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 14 synthetic order-issue handling SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
